narration: Every day, ships carry grain, oil and goods across the world.
Goods flow one way. Money flows the other.
So what does the Quran say about the economy?
Quran and Global Economy. From microeconomics to macro power: the divine blueprint of economic stability.
Detailed notes based on a Nouman Ali Khan series.

narration: Episode one. A big misconception: the separation of deen and dunya.
The common view is that religion is limited to worship, like prayer and fasting.
Business, livelihood and career are dunya, with no link to deen.
But the Quran does not reject the material world.

lines.text: The Qur'an does not reject the material world.

narration: In the Quranic view, there is no separation between spirituality and materiality.
Earning, spending and doing business are also part of worship.

lines.text: No separation between spirituality and materiality

narration: The Quran strongly criticises those who forbid themselves the lawful, good things Allah created, like beauty and rizq.
Say: who has forbidden the adornment of Allah, which He produced for His servants, and the good things of provision?

props.arabic: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِ
props.english: Say, “Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?”

narration: Cutting yourself off from the world and sitting in caves is not Islam.
So the Quran should be studied not only for creed and fiqh, like inheritance and divorce,
but also through an economic lens.
Next episode: the earth, a prison or a blessing? Follow for episode two.
